item.title: Jailed Brazil Beach Soccer Star Drawn Into Russia-US Spy Dispute
item.description: A Brazilian beach soccer star has become an unlikely bargaining chip in a dispute over an alleged Russian spy who has been sought by both Moscow and Washington.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: A Brazilian beach soccer star has become an unlikely bargaining chip in a dispute over an alleged Russian spy who has been sought by both Moscow and Washington.The Russian government is seeking a prisoner swap involving Letícia “Lelê” Villar, a Brazilian player jailed since July 2025 for bringing hashish into Russia, for Sergey Cherkasov, an alleged spy serving a five-year sentence in Brazil for using false documents, according to an official who asked not to be identified discussing private matters.Cherkasov was arrested in Brazil in 2022 after after Dutch authorities denied him entry as he sought to take up an internship at the International Criminal Court using a false Brazilian identity. In 2023, the US government charged Cherkasov, who had previously used his Brazilian passport to move to the US to pursue graduate studies at Johns Hopkins University, with acting as an agent of a Russian intelligence service and later requested his extradition.Brazilian police found no evidence that Cherkasov, who used the alias Victor Muller Ferreira, spied on the Brazilian government, companies or institutions. Brazil rejected a US request to extradite Cherkasov after its Supreme Court had approved his eventual transfer to Russia, subject to the completion of proceedings against him in Brazil. In July, the government separately ordered him expelled once he completes his Brazilian sentence or is released by the judiciary. Villar, meanwhile, has appealed directly to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for help securing her release. In a letter to Lula this month, she said “there are no words that can express or convey all the suffering, burden and pain I feel being in this place.”Brazil’s foreign affairs ministry said it has been following the situation and has been providing consular assistance to her and her family. The Justice Ministry said it doesn’t comment on ongoing cases. The Russian Embassy in Brazil and Villar’s lawyer didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.Villar, who has played for Brazil’s national team and won multiple international titles at the club level, isn’t the first prominent athlete whose detention in Russia has become entangled in a prisoner exchange. American basketball star Brittney Griner was released in a one-for-one swap in 2022 for Russian arms dealer Viktor Bout. Griner had been sentenced to nine years in prison after customs officials found vape cartridges containing cannabis oil in her luggage at a Moscow airport.Lula has cultivated a pragmatic and at times warm relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin, potentially giving Brazil room to navigate the dispute. The two leaders most recently spoke for more than an hour by phone in August.©2026 Bloomberg L.P.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

item.title: Power Outages, Flood Risks Linger as Storm Leaves East Coast
item.description: More than 400,000 homes and businesses along the East Coast are without power after an explosive storm uprooted trees in Queens and Manhattan and inundated commuter rail lines in New Jersey on Thanksgiving Day.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- More than 400,000 homes and businesses along the East Coast are without power after an explosive storm uprooted trees in Queens and Manhattan and inundated commuter rail lines in New Jersey on Thanksgiving Day.The nor’easter system that pummeled New York City and surrounding areas also carried heavy rains as far south as North Carolina. Though the storm is losing power Friday, beaches from Virginia to Maine are still at risk of coastal flooding during high tide, according to the US National Weather Service. “It was not a typical nor’easter,” said Brian Hurley, a meteorologist with the service’s Weather Prediction Center in Maryland. “It’s been a while since we saw one that had such a footprint in terms of power outages, that wasn’t tied to a tropical system.” Strong wind gusts scoured the eastern seaboard, toppling trees and knocking down power lines. Electricity is still out for more than 117,000 customers throughout Pennsylvania, according to PowerOutage.com, with over 85,000 outages in New Jersey and about 42,000 throughout New York State. The remaining outages stretch across Delaware, Maryland and Virginia. Gusty winds and lingering rain discouraged some Black Friday shoppers from waiting in line across the region. But conditions had eased considerably from the peak of the storm. Weather gauges captured gusts of up to 66 miles (106 kilometers) per hour at LaGuardia Airport in New York City Thursday evening. In Manhattan’s Central Park, top winds measured 54 miles per hour. Construction scaffolding collapsed on Central Park West and in the Bronx, according to the city’s emergency management department, while wind-blasted trees crashed through parked cars and at least one home throughout the five boroughs. Storm gusts were too strong to safely fly gigantic balloons in the iconic Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. For the first time in its history, organizers postponed the parade until Saturday morning.(Updates with new power outage numbers, damage reports starting in paragraph 1.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.
